steps.title: Orchestra
steps.say: This is Orchestra: one dashboard that runs a whole team of AI coding agents on your repository.

steps.title: You ask once
steps.say: You describe the job to one orchestrator, in plain words.

steps.title: It plans
steps.say: It reads the code, finds the cause, and splits the work into parallel tracks.

steps.title: Workers spawn
steps.say: Each track goes to its own worker, on its own git branch, so they never collide.

steps.title: Mixed models
steps.say: Mix models freely. Opus plans, Sonnet and Codex do the work, Haiku keeps the docs.

steps.title: Open any worker
steps.say: Click any worker to jump into its own chat, with its branch, context and cost.

steps.title: Report back
steps.say: You say go. The worker reports back with the files it changed and its test results.

steps.title: Review and test
steps.say: The orchestrator reviews the diff, live, and runs the whole test suite itself.

steps.title: Merge
steps.say: Only then does it merge: one squash commit per task, and nothing is deployed.

steps.title: Task board
steps.say: The task board keeps up by itself.

steps.title: Quotas unfold
steps.say: Click the quota bar, and every Claude and Codex limit unfolds.

steps.title: Quota history
steps.say: Each window keeps its history, so you see how fast it burns, week by week.

steps.title: Daily spend
steps.say: One more click opens the spend: cost per day, Claude and Codex stacked.

steps.title: Per agent
steps.say: Switch to thirty days, or break it down by agent and model.

steps.title: Limits gate
steps.say: A gate holds new workers back before a limit is hit.

steps.title: You stay in charge
steps.say: Anything risky, like moving money, waits for your OK.

steps.title: Orchestra
steps.say: Orchestra. Open source, self hosted, and it runs on the subscriptions you already have.
steps.sub: Orchestra. Open source, self-hosted, on the subscriptions you already have.
